subject: Greenline renewal — competitive bench request and proposed test roadmap
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@greenline.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenline Procurement <procurement@greenline.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal next quarter — vendor benchmark request and timeline

Hi Logan,

Renewal for our core inference usage is up on 2027-08-15 and the platform team has been asked to run a competitive evaluation. A vendor (EdgeBench) has already started a proof-of-performance with our infra team and asked for a 2-week bakeoff focused on throughput at 75% P95 latency and per-token cost under $0.002.

Before we proceed further with them, procurement asked whether Redwood can propose a formal bakeoff plan and — importantly — a commercial path if the results are positive (either term change or committed capacity uplift). We want to see:
- A lightweight test plan we can run without changing prod traffic
- Clear success metrics (latency, error rates, UNITS/hour, token cost)
- Any short-term uplift/discount options during the trial

I've attached our benchmark requirements (greenline_benchmark_requirements.pdf). Can you confirm feasibility and propose next steps this week?

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Platform, Greenline Retail

Attachments: greenline_benchmark_requirements.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@greenline.com>
Cc: Greenline Procurement <procurement@greenline.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal next quarter — vendor benchmark request and timeline

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the note and the benchmark spec. We can absolutely run a controlled bakeoff that isolates model inference performance from your prod stack. Two quick options that work for most customers:

1) Redwood-managed 2-week bakeoff: we provision a dedicated pool, run your sample workload, and produce a results report (latency percentiles, error map, token economics).
2) Short capacity trial (30 days): we route a limited percentage of real traffic under an SLA-backed trial and measure steady-state ops + long tail latencies.

I'll need a bit of input from our infra team on exact capacity sizing — attaching our sample config and runbook so you can see what we measure. Proposed next step: quick sync tomorrow to confirm which option Greenline prefers and the dataset to use.

Attaching: redwood_bakeoff-sample-config.yml, redwood_bakeoff-runbook.pdf

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Greenline renewal — benchmark request (internal)

Team — putting this on your radar. Greenline sent benchmark requirements and procurement wants a formal plan this week. Renewal date 2027-08-15. External asked for 2-week bakeoff target (P95 latency @ 75% throughput, token cost target).

Ask:
- Karthik: can you confirm whether the dedicated 2-week footprint below is realistic from a capacity/ops perspective? If so, estimate GPU hours and any uplift we should include for steady-state testing.
- Marissa: suggest commercial levers we can offer as a short-term preservation to win the renewal (one-off uplift credits, temporary committed-tier pricing, performance-based credits).
- Grace: will need a short ops SLA template and runbook sign-off so we can run with minimal legal friction.

I'm proposing: 2-week Redwood-managed bakeoff + a 60-day post-trial uplift window where Greenline can commit to a reserved pool for 6 months at a promotional rate if targets are met. Attach SOW outline and runbook. Keep proposed commercial concessions conservative; we'll escalate if procurement pushes hard.

Attachments: SOW-burst-capacity-draft.pdf, redwood_bakeoff-runbook.pdf

Logan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Greenline renewal — benchmark request (internal)

Agree with the approach. Quick commercial framework I recommend:

- Offer: 2-week managed bakeoff (no charge) + 60-day trial of uplifted capacity at promotional rates.
- Pricing concession: 15% off list on new committed capacity if signed within 45 days of successful bakeoff.
- Overages: first month of overage billed at 30% discount to give them breathing room while they ramp.
- Performance credit: if P95 latency exceeds agreed metric during first 30 days post-commit, provide credits up to 5% of monthly invoice.

Risks: competitor might promise deeper up-front discounts. We defend by making the bakeoff results and runbook public within Greenline procurement + a clear SLO -> credit mechanism that shows we’re confident in performance.

If Karthik confirms cost of the dedicated pool, we can draft the SOW and present commercial bullets to Priya tomorrow.

-Marissa
Head of Retention, Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@greenline.com>
Cc: Greenline Procurement <procurement@greenline.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal next quarter — vendor benchmark request and timeline

Hi Priya —

Great to connect. Based on your requirements, attached is the proposed bakeoff roadmap and a short SOW for the dedicated trial. High level:

1) Baseline (2 business days): run your sample traces against a baseline model in a secure, isolated environment; confirm workload shape
2) Load phase (3 days): ramp to target throughput and measure latency percentiles, error rates, and token economics
3) Steady-state (10 days): sustained run at target throughput to capture long-tail behavior and ops stability
4) Report & recommendation (2 days): detailed results, cost per token analysis, and recommended committed-capacity tiers

Success metrics (proposed): P95 latency <= your target (75% throughput baseline), error rate < 0.5%, token cost within agreed range. If metrics are met, we propose the following commercial path: 15% off committed capacity for a 6-month reserved pool (must be signed within 45 days), plus a 30% overage discount for month 1 of the transition. We’ll include a performance-based credit clause in the SOW.

Logistics: we can start the bakeoff as soon as you provide the sample traces and a short dataplane allowlist. Proposed start: week of 06/07. If that works, I'll share a draft SOW and a DocuSign link for the trial acceptance.

Attachments: redwood_bakeoff-runbook.pdf, SOW-burst-capacity-draft.pdf
Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/GL-2026-REN-17

Would you be available for a 30-min kickoff tomorrow at 10am PT?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199
